keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "It flourished between 4400 and 4000 BC" (infobox "circa 5,000 B.C. - circa 4,000 B.C."); the core is the 30 km reach of the east bank between Matmar and Qau in the Asyut Governorate. Related finds "farther to the south at" Mahgar Dendera, Armant, Elkab and Nekhen and in the Wadi Hammamat are find spots and are not drawn. No area figure to compare.

ledger.note: 4400 BCE: the Badarian farmers of the Asyut reach, the first Predynastic culture of Upper Egypt. "It flourished between 4400 and 4000 BC" and "might have already emerged by 5000 BC"; the Tasian is "Contemporary" on the infobox; the lead's 4400 BC is used and the infobox's 5000 BC noted.

region.text: El-Badari "between Matmar and Qau": the area "stretches for 30 km (19 mi) along the east bank of the Nile", "approximately 200 km (120 mi) northwest of present-day Luxor"; Mostagedda, Deir Tasa, Hemamieh

ledger.note: 4000 BCE: the Badarian becomes the Amratian, Naqada I. Infobox "Followed by: Amratian culture"; the Naqada page dates Naqada I "about 3900-3650 BC" and the Naqada culture from c. 4000 BC.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: one radius on the Nile around the Badari cemeteries, never a frontier.

sources.title: Badarian culture
sources.note: Dates 4400-4000 BC (infobox 5000-4000), the Matmar-Qau reach, the related southern finds, the Amratian succession.

notes: Culture dossier, one page. Disagreement: start 4400 BC (lead) vs 5000 BC (infobox); 4400 BCE is used, leaving Upper Egypt empty before it (the Tasian culture, contemporary and undated, has no dossier). Gazetteer: El-Badari, Qau el-Kebir, Matmar, Mostagedda are not places; a 70 km radius around Asyut stands in.
